features

Every part of Fez,
shown one by one.

This is the complete working surface: component files, templates, state, props, directives, CSS, motion, lifecycle hooks, instance helpers, static APIs, the DOM differ, Pjax and CLI tools. Every item pairs the rule with a small example and the result it produces.

Components State & props Templates Directives & slots CSS & motion Lifecycle Core methods Runtime APIs DOM & performance Pjax & tooling

01 / 10

Components and loading

A component is a browser-native custom element described by one readable file. Load it directly, inline it, or register it from JavaScript.

.fez · no build step

Single-file components

Module imports, class logic, scoped and global styles, documentation, demo markup and the template can live together. The browser compiler handles the file directly.

<info>A friendly card.</info>
<demo><hello-card name="Ada" /></demo>

<script>
  class {}
</script>

<style>
  padding: 12px;
  b { color: #c8102e; }
</style>

Hello, <b>{props.name}</b>.
Hello, Ada.
compiled in the browser - no JSX, bundler or generated source folder

script fez · template fez · Fez.head · JSON template

Load components and their input

Use a script fez tag for a file, an inline xmp or template definition, or Fez.head() when the path is discovered at runtime. A preceding JSON template can supply large server-rendered props without putting them in an attribute.

<script fez="./fez/ui-card.fez"></script>

<xmp fez="inline-badge">
  <style>padding: 4px 8px;</style>
  <slot />
</xmp>

Fez.head({ fez: './fez/ui-dialog.fez' })

<script type="application/json">
  {"name":"Ada","roles":["admin"]}
</script>
<user-card data-json-template="true" />
ui-card readyinline-badge readyui-dialog readyJSON props parsed
definitions join one registry; JSON input passes through the same PROPS schema

Custom Elements · NAME

Native tags, semantic roots

Use the component as a real custom element. NAME chooses the rendered root, so a navigation component can become a genuine nav instead of a permanent wrapper.

<script>
  class {
    NAME = 'nav'
  }
</script>

<a href="/">Home</a>

<site-nav></site-nav>
<nav class="fez fez-site-nav">...</nav>
custom-element ergonomics with ordinary, stylable output

imports · head assets · import maps

A module zone before the class

Imports, shared constants and Fez.head() calls live before the component class. Import maps keep bare specifiers consistent across components; scripts and styles are deduplicated in head.

<script>
  Fez.head({ importmap: {
    three: 'https://esm.sh/three@0.180.0'
  }})
  Fez.head({ css: './map.css' })

  import * as THREE from 'three'
  const sceneColor = '#17181c'

  class { onMount() { /* use THREE */ } }
</script>
one shared module URL and one injected stylesheet
the class stays last; module-level work runs once per definition

META · info · demo · Fez.index

Documentation travels with the component

META, <info>, <demo> and raw source are indexed beside the class. Demo browsers and tooling can discover everything without a parallel manifest.

<info>Compact user avatar.</info>
<demo><ui-avatar name="Ada" /></demo>

<script>
  class { META = { category: 'identity' } }
</script>

Fez.index.get('ui-avatar')
Fez.index.withDemo()
classmetainfodemosource
one unified entry powers docs, demos and inspection

GLOBAL = true · GLOBAL = 'Name'

Singleton components

Global overlays, toast hosts and dialogs can append themselves to body exactly once. A string also exposes the instance on window for calls from ordinary page code.

<script>
  class {
    GLOBAL = 'Dialog'

    open(message) {
      this.state.message = message
    }
  }
</script>

Dialog.open('Saved')
Saved  - one dialog instance in body
GLOBAL = true keeps the singleton without creating a window handle

components.txt · built-in components

Load a whole component library

A text file can list relative or absolute component paths. Fez also ships fez-component, fez-include, fez-inline and fez-demo for dynamic components, remote HTML, inline reactivity and catalogue pages.

# one component per line
ui-button
ui-dialog
forms/input-date
/shared/app-shell

Fez.head({ fez: './components.txt' })

<fez-component name="ui-button" />
<fez-include src="./partial.html" />
<fez-demo src="./components.txt" />
4 pathsresolved, fetched, compiled and indexed
extensions are optional; nested paths resolve from the list file

02 / 10

State and props

Reactive values are explicit: local UI goes in state, shared values in globalState, durable non-render data in local, and input from the parent in props.

this.state · fezReactiveStore · deep reactivity · batching

Assign state, get a render

Object and array mutations are observed deeply. Multiple writes in the same tick collapse into one animation-frame render, so ordinary JavaScript assignment is the full state API.

init() {
  this.state.user = { name: 'Ada' }
  this.state.tags = ['fast']
}

update() {
  this.state.user.name = 'Grace'
  this.state.tags.push('small')
  this.state.ready = true
}

makeDraft() {
  const draft = this.fezReactiveStore(
    { query: '' },
    (object, key, value) => audit(key, value),
    { shallow: true },
  )
  draft.query = 'Fez'
}
one renderGrace · fast, small · ready
three writes, one batched DOM morph

this.local

Non-reactive instance storage

Editors, charts, cached measurements, timers and normalized callbacks belong in local. Writes do not render, and Fez clears the store after onDestroy().

onMount() {
  this.local.chart = new Chart(this.canvas)
  this.local.last_width = this.root.offsetWidth
}

resize() {
  this.local.last_width = this.root.offsetWidth
}
0 rendersexternal objects stay outside the template cycle
per-instance, non-reactive and automatically discarded

this.props · parent updates

Props remain live

Templates read props.name; methods read this.props.name. Top-level prop assignments render and flow to children, while nested object identity is preserved.

<h3>{props.user.name}</h3>
<child-card :user="props.user" />

rename(name) {
  this.props.user = {
    ...this.props.user,
    name
  }
}
Gracesame object passed to the child
do not copy changing props into state

PROPS · runtime coercion

Typed HTML attributes

The schema accepts String, Number, Boolean, Array, Object, Function, Date and custom casters. Values arrive typed before init().

PROPS = {
  title: String,
  page: Number,
  open: Boolean,
  items: Array,
  user: Object,
  on_pick: Function,
  since: Date,
  slug: raw => String(raw).toLowerCase(),
}

<ui-pager page="3" open items='["a","b"]' />
page: 3open: trueitems: Array(2)
no manual parseInt, JSON.parse or boolean string checks

default · required · enum · transform · state

Validation and state seeding

Defaults recover missing or invalid values, required reports omissions, enum limits choices, a one-argument default transforms raw input, and state seeds component-owned reactive data once.

PROPS = {
  size: {
    type: String,
    default: 'md',
    enum: ['sm', 'md', 'lg'],
  },
  tags: {
    type: Array,
    state: true,
    default: raw => (raw || '').split(','),
  },
  user: { type: Object, required: true },
}
size = mdstate.tags = [...]errors route through Fez.onError
state seeding copies arrays and plain objects shallowly

:prop · data-props · Fez.getFunction

Pass real values and callbacks

A colon attribute parks objects, arrays, booleans and functions without stringifying them. data-props accepts a JSON object, and handler props normalize through Fez.getFunction().

<user-card
  :user="state.current_user"
  :active="true"
  :on_pick="fez.pick"
/>

<user-card data-props='{"name":"Ada"}' />

init(props) {
  this.local.on_pick = Fez.getFunction(props.on_pick)
}
Object identity keptFunction callable
plain attributes stay strings; colon attributes stay JavaScript values

this.globalState · Fez.state · fez-inline

Shared reactive state

Reading a global key subscribes only that component. Writes notify onGlobalStateChange immediately and batch the required renders. Static HTML can join through fez-inline.

increment() {
  this.globalState.count =
    (this.globalState.count || 0) + 1
}

Fez.state.get('count')
Fez.state.set('count', 4)
Fez.state.subscribe('count', (value, old) => {})
Fez.state.subscribe((key, value, old) => {})
Fez.state.forEach('count', component => {})
Fez.state.createProxy(component)

<fez-inline>Count: {globalState.count}</fez-inline>
Count: 4only readers of count refresh
global state subscriptions are tracked and cleaned automatically

03 / 10

Template language

Fez templates stay close to HTML: braces for values, explicit blocks for control flow, and ordinary JavaScript expressions where a value belongs.

{expression} · attributes

Escaped expressions

Read state, props, local, globalState and component methods in text or attributes. Text is HTML-escaped and expression attributes are quoted automatically.

<h2>{props.title}</h2>
<p>{state.user.name.toUpperCase()}</p>
<input value={state.query} />
<div data-count={state.items.length}></div>
TEAMADA · data-count="3"
write attr={value}; the compiler supplies safe quotes

{@html} · {@json}

Raw HTML and JSON output

{@html} deliberately inserts trusted markup without escaping. {@json} produces a readable JSON debug block for any value.

<div>{@html state.trusted_html}</div>

{@json state.user}
Formatted content
{"name":"Ada","active":true}
use raw HTML only with content you already trust

{@block name} · {@block:name}

Reusable template blocks

Define a small template fragment once and render it by name. Blocks share the template context, so they can read the same props, state and methods.

{@block avatar}
  <img src={props.avatar} alt={props.name} />
{/block}

<header>{@block:avatar}<h3>{props.name}</h3></header>
<footer>{@block:avatar}</footer>
avatar rendered twiceone block definition
named fragments avoid copying repeated template markup

{#if} · {:else if} · {:else}

Conditional branches

Use a readable block for alternate HTML trees. Closing and opening states produce genuinely different markup, which keeps the differ and render hash correct.

{#if state.status === 'loading'}
  <p>Loading...</p>
{:else if state.status === 'error'}
  <p class="error">Try again.</p>
{:else}
  <p>Ready.</p>
{/if}
Ready.
only the matching branch reaches the DOM

{#unless} · Fez truthiness

Empty-aware negative conditions

unless is the inverse of if. In Fez, empty arrays and empty objects are also falsy, alongside null, undefined, false, zero and an empty string.

{#unless state.results}
  <p>No results found.</p>
{/unless}

// all render the empty branch
state.results = []
state.results = {}
state.results = null
No results found.
non-empty arrays and objects are truthy

{#await} · {:then} · {:catch}

Promises in templates

Assign the Promise itself to state. The template shows pending markup immediately, then refreshes automatically for the resolved value or error.

init() {
  this.state.user = Fez.fetch('/api/user')
}

{#await state.user}
  <p>Loading user...</p>
{:then user}
  <p>Hello, {user.name}.</p>
{:catch error}
  <p>Failed: {error.message}</p>
{/await}

// low-level equivalent
Fez.fezAwait(promise, { pending, then, catch })
pendingthenorcatch
assign a fresh Promise to show the loading branch again

{#each} · implicit i · explicit index

Array loops

each exposes an implicit i, or an explicit index after the item name. A stable key preserves identity when items move.

<ol>
  {#each state.users as user, index}
    <li key={user.id}>
      {index + 1}. {user.name}
    </li>
  {/each}
</ol>

{#each state.tags as tag}
  <span>{i}: {tag}</span>
{/each}
1. Ada2. Grace3. Linus
keys let the differ move the existing node instead of replacing it

{#for} · arrays · objects · null safety

Collection and object loops

for accepts arrays and objects. Two parameters mean value/index for arrays and key/value for objects; brackets are optional. Null and undefined behave as empty collections.

{#for item in state.items}
  <span>{item}</span>
{/for}

{#for key, value in state.settings}
  <div>{key}: {value}</div>
{/for}

{#for [value, index] in state.items}
  <span>{index}: {value}</span>
{/for}
theme: darkdensity: compact
Fez.toPairs() supplies the same pair model to both loop forms

{:else} in loops

Empty-list fallbacks

An else branch belongs directly to each or for, so loading an empty collection does not need a separate conditional.

{#each state.notifications as note}
  <article key={note.id}>{note.text}</article>
{:else}
  <p class="empty">You are all caught up.</p>
{/each}
You are all caught up.
works for [], {}, null and undefined

ternary attributes · class:name

Dynamic attributes and classes

Use a normal expression or ternary inside attributes. The class:name directive merges conditional classes without overwriting the static class list.

<button
  class="btn"
  class:active={state.active}
  class:loading={state.loading}
  disabled={state.loading ? 'disabled' : ''}
  aria-label={state.active ? 'Deactivate' : 'Activate'}
>Save</button>
class="btn active"
control-flow blocks are never placed inside an attribute

inline handlers · arrows · strict !

Three event-handler forms

String handlers are concise for scalar values. Arrow handlers capture complex loop objects. Appending ! fires only on the element itself and also prevents default and stops propagation.

<button onclick="fez.save()">Save</button>
<input onchange="fez.rename(this.value)" />

{#each state.tasks as task}
  <button onclick={() => edit(task)}>Edit</button>
{/each}

<div class="overlay" onclick!="fez.close()">
  <button>Does not close overlay</button>
</div>
scalar inlineobject capturedstrict target
arrow functions are compiled into stable Fez handler slots

self-closing custom tags · legacy syntax

HTML correction and legacy templates

Self-closing custom elements are expanded to valid paired tags before the browser can mis-nest them. Older double-brace expressions, conditions and loops remain supported for existing components.

<ui-icon name="star" />
<user-card :user="state.user" />

// legacy, still supported
{{ state.name }}
{{if state.open}}...{{else}}...{{/if}}
{{for item in state.items}}...{{/for}}
<ui-icon name="star"></ui-icon>
new code uses the single-brace Svelte-like syntax

04 / 10

Directives, slots and forms

Special fez: attributes connect template nodes to component behavior without hiding the resulting DOM.

fez:bind

Two-way form binding

Bind an input, select or textarea to state when the component should re-render as the value changes. The directive updates the target path and schedules the render.

init() {
  this.state.volume = 40
}

<input type="range" min="0" max="100"
       fez:bind="state.volume" />
<output>{state.volume}%</output>
40%
for large forms, prefer fez:this and read values only on submit

fez:this · stable auto-ID

Direct element references

fez:this exposes the live node on the component instance after render. Static reference names also receive a stable generated ID, helping the differ preserve typed values and focus.

<input fez:this="name_input" />

submit() {
  const name = this.name_input.value
}

// generated automatically
// id="fez-42-name_input"
this.name_inputpoints to the preserved input node
refs are ready in onMount(), not init()

fez:use

Run a DOM hook on insertion

A use directive calls a component method or inline function with the inserted node. It is the focused escape hatch for setup that belongs to one element.

<input fez:use="focusInput" />
<canvas fez:use="node => mountChart(node)" />

focusInput(node) {
  node.focus()
}
input focused when its node is added
the callback receives the actual live DOM element

fez:class

Delayed classes

Add a class immediately or after a millisecond delay. This is useful when a CSS transition needs the initial frame to paint before its active class appears.

<span fez:class="visible:100">Ready</span>

<style>
  span { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .2s; }
  span.visible { opacity: 1; }
</style>
+ visible after 100ms
for full enter and leave animation, use fez:in and fez:out

fez:keep · key · child isolation

Preserve DOM identity

A stable key tells the differ to keep and move the same plain element. Child Fez components are isolated automatically; wrap one in a keyed plain element when the parent also controls its identity.

{#each state.users as user}
  <article key={user.id} fez:keep="user-{user.id}">
    <user-card :user="user" />
  </article>
{/each}

<input fez:keep="search-input" />
focus keptcomponent state keptnode moved
fez:keep belongs on plain HTML, never directly on a Fez component

slot · slot unwrap · fezSlot

Slots that preserve listeners

A normal slot keeps children in a .fez-slot wrapper. unwrap dissolves that wrapper into the parent. Fez moves the real nodes, so existing listeners survive.

<section class="panel">
  <slot />
</section>

// or direct children, no wrapper
<nav><slot unwrap /></nav>

// low-level equivalent
this.fezSlot(source, target)
default wrapperordirect children
slot unwrap components render once and cannot use reactive state

onSubmit · formData()

Forms become plain objects

If a component owns or sits inside a form, onSubmit(data) receives its named fields automatically. Call formData() directly when submission is controlled elsewhere.

onSubmit({ name, role }) {
  this.save({ name, role })
}

saveDraft() {
  const data = this.formData()
}

<form>
  <input name="name" value="Ada" />
  <select name="role">...</select>
</form>
{ name: 'Ada', role: 'admin' }
Fez locates the closest parent or first child form

05 / 10

CSS and motion

Scoping is explicit, nesting is built in, responsive and theme rules stay compact, and Web Animations power enter, leave, reorder and size changes.

style · wrapper & · nested selectors

Scoped, nested component CSS

Every rule in <style> is scoped to the generated component class. Root declarations style the wrapper; & addresses it explicitly; nested selectors flatten to ordinary CSS.

<style>
  padding: 18px;          /* component wrapper */

  &:hover { border-color: #c8102e; }

  article {
    display: grid;
    h3 { margin: 0; }
    a:hover { color: #c8102e; }
  }
</style>
.fez-ui-cardcontains every emitted selector
no CSS Modules, Sass compiler or shadow DOM required

style global · :global(...)

Two deliberate global escapes

A <style global> block is emitted document-wide and deduplicated. Inside scoped CSS, :global(selector) hoists just one rule for a third-party node outside the component.

<style>
  .toolbar { display: flex; }
  :global(.mapboxgl-popup) { z-index: 20; }
</style>

<style global>
  :root { --brand: #c8102e; }
  .app-shell { min-height: 100vh; }
</style>
scoped channelglobal channel
scope is declared on the style tag, never guessed from selectors

@keyframes · @font-face · @property

Legal at-rules from scoped files

Rules that cannot legally nest inside a component selector are hoisted automatically. Media, supports and container rules remain nested around the scoped selector.

<style>
  .notice { animation: enter .25s ease-out; }

  @keyframes enter {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px); }
    to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
  }

  @media (min-width: 800px) {
    .notice { padding: 20px; }
  }
</style>
@keyframes hoisted@media stays scoped
font-face and property definitions follow the same legal-CSS rule

:mobile · :tablet · :desktop

Responsive style macros

Built-in macros expand wherever they are nested: mobile is up to 767px, tablet is 768-1023px, and desktop begins at 1200px. @include name is an equivalent spelling.

<style>
  .grid {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);

    :tablet { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }
    :mobile { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  }

  :desktop { max-width: 1200px; }
  @include mobile { padding: 12px; }
</style>
mobile: 1tablet: 2desktop: 3
the space before { is required for macro expansion

:dark · zero specificity

Dark mode without a theme runtime

The dark macro matches any component under html.dark using zero-specificity :where(). Toggle the class yourself, or redefine the macro to follow the operating system.

<style>
  .card {
    color: #17181c;
    background: #fff;
    :dark { color: #eee; background: #17181c; }
  }
</style>

document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', true)

// optional OS-driven behavior
Fez.cssMixin('dark',
  '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)')
Dark card
put the class on html so root tokens and overscroll match too

cssMixin · globalCss · cssClass · extractCss · color helpers

Programmable CSS utilities

Register selector or at-rule macros, inject deduplicated global nested CSS, create a generated utility class, and extract every injected rule in order for debugging or server rendering.

Fez.cssMixin('motion-ok',
  '@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')

Fez.globalCss('.toast { &.error { color: red } }')

const klass = Fez.cssClass('display: grid; gap: 12px;')
const allCss = Fez.extractCss()

Fez.darkenColor('#c8102e', 15)
Fez.lightenColor('#c8102e', 15)
:motion-okdeduped sheetgenerated classcolor shades
the same flattener handles component and runtime CSS

fez:in · fez:out · fez:transition

Enter and leave transitions

Intro runs when a plain element appears. Outro delays removal until animation completes. fez:transition applies one spec both ways, while explicit in or out attributes can override either direction.

{#if state.open}
  <div
    fez:in="fly, from=bottom, duration=280"
    fez:out="fade, duration=140"
  >Saved</div>
{/if}

<div fez:transition="pop, duration=220">Menu</div>
insertfly inremovefade, then detach
duration, delay and easing work on every transition

fade · fly · slide · scale · pop · blur · flip · rotate · draw

Nine built-in transitions

Cover opacity, directional movement, accordion layout, scaling, overshoot, blur, 3D flips, rotation and SVG stroke drawing. Named Svelte-style easings and CSS timing functions are both accepted.

<div fez:in="fade">...</div>
<div fez:in="fly, from=left, distance=30">...</div>
<div fez:in="slide, axis=x">...</div>
<div fez:in="scale, start=.7">...</div>
<div fez:in="pop, easing=backOut">...</div>
<div fez:in="blur, amount=8">...</div>
<div fez:in="flip, axis=y">...</div>
<div fez:in="rotate, angle=-120">...</div>
<path fez:in="draw, speed=2" />
9 effectsnamed easingreduced motion safe
non-SVG draw targets fall back to fade

Fez.transitions · CSS @keyframes names

Custom transition functions

Add a transition factory to the registry and return keyframes plus timing. An unknown transition name falls back to a CSS @keyframes animation of that name.

Fez.transitions.wobble = (node, params) => ({
  keyframes: [
    { transform: 'rotate(-4deg)', opacity: 0 },
    { transform: 'none', opacity: 1 },
  ],
  duration: params.duration || 240,
  easing: 'backOut',
})

<div fez:in="wobble, duration=300">Hello</div>
<div fez:in="my-css-keyframes">Hello</div>
registry functionorCSS animation name
first keyframe is hidden; last frame is the natural state

fez:animate="flip"

Animate list reordering

FLIP measures keyed nodes before and after the morph, then animates the position delta. Insertions can use fez:in; removals can use fez:out.

{#each state.items as item}
  <li
    key={item.id}
    fez:animate="flip, duration=250"
    fez:in="fly, from=left"
    fez:out="fade, duration=140"
  >{item.name}</li>
{/each}
insert fliesreorder glidesremove fades
identity is required so the differ can recognize a moved node

height · width · size · Fez.animateSize

Animate content size

A ResizeObserver animates a kept element from its old box to its new one, including changes caused by nested components or outside DOM code. Combine size and FLIP specs when both change.

<div fez:animate="height, duration=250">
  {#if state.open}
    <p>Expandable content</p>
  {/if}
</div>

<li fez:animate="flip, height">...</li>

Fez.animateSize(node, 'width, duration=180')
heightwidthboth axes
inline dimensions and overflow are restored after animation

06 / 10

Lifecycle hooks

Every lifecycle moment has a named method. Use only the hooks the component needs; Fez supplies empty implementations for the rest.

init(props)

Initialize before rendering

init runs once after props are coerced and before the first template render. Initialize every reactive state key here; original slot children are still present, but template refs are not.

init(props) {
  this.state.count = props.start || 0
  this.state.open = false
  this.local.on_save = Fez.getFunction(props.on_save)
}
props typedstate readytemplate has not rendered yet
PROPS state seeding happens just before init

beforeRender()

Compute derived state

This hook runs immediately before every render, including the first. Derive values from current state and props here so templates never see stale calculations.

beforeRender() {
  this.state.full_name =
    `${this.state.first} ${this.state.last}`
  this.state.total = this.state.items.reduce(
    (sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0
  )
}
Ada LovelaceTotal: $48
the Fez replacement for reactive declarations and computed stores

onMount(props)

Work with the rendered DOM

onMount runs once after the first DOM render. Template refs, layout measurements, focus and third-party libraries belong here.

onMount(props) {
  this.name_input.focus()
  this.local.editor = new Editor({
    element: this.editor_root,
  })
}

<input fez:this="name_input" />
<div fez:this="editor_root"></div>
refs point to connected, rendered elements
external library instances stay in this.local

afterRender()

React after every morph

This hook runs after the rendered HTML has been applied. Use it for a small side effect that genuinely needs the latest DOM after every component render.

afterRender() {
  this.root.style.setProperty(
    '--rows',
    this.root.querySelectorAll('li').length
  )
}
DOM morphed--rows: 6 applied afterward
avoid state writes here unless a second render is intentional

onRefresh(props)

Know when a parent preserves you

onRefresh runs after mount and whenever a parent render keeps this child component. It does not fire for the child's own state render or for outside DOM events.

onRefresh(props) {
  if (props.revision !== this.local.revision) {
    this.local.revision = props.revision
    this.refresh()
  }
}
parent morphedchild instance stayed connected
use this.on for document, window and Pjax events

onPropsChange(name, value)

Observe changed attributes

Called when an original attribute is added or changed. Declared schema values are already coerced, so the hook receives the same types as init.

PROPS = { page: Number }

onPropsChange(name, value) {
  if (name === 'page') {
    console.log(value, typeof value)
  }
}

element.setAttribute('page', '4')
4, "number"
undeclared props continue to arrive as strings

onStateChange(key, value, oldValue)

Observe local state writes

Runs when reactive local state changes, with the top-level key and old and new values. The pending UI render remains batched into the next frame.

onStateChange(key, value, oldValue) {
  if (key === 'count') {
    this.globalState.max = Math.max(
      value,
      this.globalState.max || 0
    )
  }
}
count: 2 → 3global max becomes 3
nested writes report through their owning top-level state key

onGlobalStateChange(key, value, oldValue)

Observe shared state

Components that read a global key receive this hook synchronously when that key changes. Their render is scheduled once alongside any local state changes.

init() {
  this.globalState.theme // subscribe by reading
}

onGlobalStateChange(key, value, oldValue) {
  if (key === 'theme') {
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle(
      'dark', value === 'dark'
    )
  }
}
theme: light → darksubscribers update together
a component's own write during render does not schedule an extra pass

addOnDestroy() · onDestroy()

Release external resources

When MutationObserver sees the component disconnect, Fez runs callbacks registered with addOnDestroy(), removes listeners, observers, timers and subscriptions, then calls onDestroy for external resources.

onDestroy() {
  this.local.editor?.destroy()
  this.local.chart?.dispose()
}

onMount() {
  const observer = new MutationObserver(this.track)
  observer.observe(this.root, { childList: true })
  this.addOnDestroy(() => observer.disconnect())
}

// already cleaned by Fez:
// this.on(...)
// this.setTimeout(...)
// this.setInterval(...)
// this.subscribe(...)
listeners removedtimers clearedlocal cleared
cleanup runs once, even if the node is removed more than once

07 / 10

Core instance methods

Every component keeps direct access to its live root, focused DOM shortcuts, rendering controls, safe events, timers and component-level communication.

root · find · val

Read and write the live DOM

root is the mounted component element. find() scopes a selector to it. val() gets or sets form values, checked state, or innerHTML for non-form nodes.

const button = this.find('button.save')
const query = this.val('input[name=search]')

this.val('input[name=search]', 'Fez')
this.val('.preview', '<b>Ready</b>')

this.root.append(document.createElement('hr'))
scoped queryinput valuelive DOM write
Fez does not hide or replace browser DOM APIs

this.n()

Build native nodes in JavaScript

The built-in node builder accepts a tag, dot-separated classes, attributes and text or child nodes. Functions become bound DOM properties, boolean attributes follow HTML rules, and arrays append every child.

const save = this.n('button.primary', {
  type: 'button',
  disabled: false,
  onclick: this.save,
}, 'Save')

const row = this.n('.actions', [
  save,
  this.n('span.hint', 'Ready'),
])

this.root.append(row)
Ready
this.n('.actions', ...) defaults to a div with class="actions"

attr · prop · copy

Attributes and DOM properties

attr() gets or sets a root attribute. prop() resolves an original property or prop and binds functions. copy() forwards chosen input props to the semantic root.

init() {
  this.copy('href', 'target', 'aria-label')
  this.attr('data-ready', 'true')

  const click = this.prop('onclick')
  click?.()
}

// <smart-link href="/docs" target="_blank" />
<a href="/docs" target="_blank" data-ready="true">
non-string values copied by copy() land as DOM properties

addClass · toggleClass · setStyle

Focused presentation helpers

Add several classes, toggle one with an optional force value, or set one or many CSS custom properties and styles on the root.

this.addClass('ready compact')
this.addClass('selected', this.find('li'))

this.toggleClass('open')
this.toggleClass('disabled', this.props.disabled)

this.setStyle('--accent', '#c8102e')
this.setStyle({ color: 'white', background: '#17181c' })
ready compact · --accent set
pass a node to class helpers; setStyle targets the component root

rootId · UID · fezName · fezHtmlRoot · isConnected

Stable identity and connection state

rootId() returns the existing root ID or assigns a unique one. isConnected reports whether the component root is currently attached to the document.

onMount() {
  const id = this.rootId()
  console.log(id)             // fez_42
  console.log(this.UID)       // 42
  console.log(this.fezName)   // user-card
  console.log(this.fezHtmlRoot) // Fez(42).
  console.log(this.isConnected) // true
}
fez_42connected
late async callbacks can check connection before touching the page

childNodes · childObjects · dissolve

Work with original children

Read child elements as nodes, map them, or turn them into objects containing HTML, root references, node names and attributes. dissolve() removes the component wrapper while keeping its children.

const nodes = this.childNodes()
const labels = this.childNodes(node => node.textContent)
const objects = this.childObjects()
// [{ html, ROOT, NODE_NAME, title, ...attrs }]

const moved = this.dissolve()

// or replace the wrapper with a semantic node
this.dissolve(document.createElement('nav'))
nodesmapped valuesobjectsunwrapped
child node references remain the real nodes throughout

refresh · fezRefresh · fezRender · fezParseHtml · fezNextTick

Rendering controls

refresh() and fezRefresh() schedule the normal render. fezRender() can render the configured template or supplied content. fezNextTick() deduplicates named work into the next animation frame.

this.refresh()
this.fezRefresh()

this.fezRender()
this.fezRender('<p>Temporary markup</p>')

const parsed = this.fezParseHtml(templateText)

this.fezNextTick(() => {
  this.measureLayout()
}, 'measure-layout')
one next-frame rendernamed work deduped
normal state and prop assignments already schedule refresh automatically

on · onWindowResize · onWindowScroll · onElementResize

Auto-cleaned event listeners

on() binds this, guards disconnected instances, supports throttling and returns a disposer. The resize and scroll shortcuts call once immediately; element resize uses ResizeObserver.

const off = this.on('pjax:render', this.followPage)
this.on(window, 'keydown', this.onKey)
this.on(this.root, 'pointermove', this.move, { throttle: 50 })

this.onWindowResize(this.layout, 100)
this.onWindowScroll(this.markSection, 80)
this.onElementResize(this.panel, this.fit, 120)

Fez.WINDOW_EVENTS.add('app:layout')

off() // optional early removal
windowdocumentany EventTargetResizeObserver
known window events default to window; all other string events default to document

setTimeout · setInterval

Timers that cannot outlive a component

Both helpers skip callbacks after disconnect and clear themselves during destruction. Named intervals replace an earlier interval with the same purpose.

this.setTimeout(() => {
  this.state.saved = false
}, 1200)

this.setInterval(() => {
  this.state.now = new Date()
}, 1000, 'clock')

// a second interval named "clock" replaces the first
timeout trackedinterval trackedboth cleared on destroy
use these instead of manual window timer cleanup

publish · subscribe

Component-level messaging

A component publish walks up through parent components until a matching subscriber handles it. Subscriptions clean up automatically and return an unsubscribe function.

// child
select(user) {
  this.publish('user-selected', user)
}

// parent
init() {
  this.subscribe('user-selected', user => {
    this.state.selected = user
  })
}
child publishes→nearest parent handles
use Fez.publish for a document-wide broadcast instead

Fetch with parsing and cache

Promise and callback forms support GET query params and POST FormData. JSON parses automatically, GET responses cache in memory, and simultaneous identical requests share one in-flight Promise.

Fez.localStorage

Typed local storage

Values serialize and parse as JSON, so numbers, booleans, arrays and objects retain their types. Missing keys can return a caller-supplied fallback.

Fez.localStorage.set('count', 42)

Fez.localStorage.set('user', { name: 'Ada' })

Fez.publish · Fez.subscribe

Global pub/sub with targeting

Broadcast to every subscriber, or attach a subscriber to a node or selector so it fires only while that target is connected. Every subscribe call returns an unsubscribe function.

const off = Fez.subscribe('signed-in', user => {})

Fez.subscribe(node, 'refresh', callback)
Fez.subscribe('#modal', 'refresh', callback)

Fez.publish('refresh')

broadcastconnected node onlylive selector only

Create a root from HTML, build encoded tags, escape text, activate one sibling, or invoke the component-aware DOM differ directly. nodeMorph also accepts fragments and advanced matching options.

const root = Fez.domRoot('<section>Hello</section>')

09 / 10

DOM and performance

Fez renders HTML, then carefully morphs the live DOM. Components and important nodes keep their identity, and large specialized widgets can opt into direct DOM speed.

real DOM morph · component boundaries

A component-aware differ

There is no virtual DOM. The rendered string becomes real nodes and morphs the existing tree. Child Fez components are moved and receive prop refreshes, but their internal DOM and state are never morphed by the parent.

// parent changes its own state
this.state.heading = 'Updated'

<h2>{state.heading}</h2>
<user-card :user="state.user" />

// result:
// h2 text is morphed
// user-card instance is preserved
// only changed props reach the child
parent DOM patchedchild state keptfocus kept
server HTML and external DOM remain first-class citizens

fez:keep · fez-key · key · id · source signature

Priority-based node matching

The differ prefers explicit identity, then stable IDs and source signatures, with a scored soft-match fallback. Reordering can therefore move existing nodes instead of destroying them.

1. fez:keep="invoice-7"
2. fez-key="invoice-7"
3. key="invoice-7"
4. id="invoice-7"
5. matching element source/signature
6. scored soft match

<li key={invoice.id}>{invoice.total}</li>
same nodemoves from row 4 to row 1
strong identity also enables reliable FLIP animation

FNV-1 hash · render slots · requestAnimationFrame

Two levels of render skipping

State and prop writes batch into one frame. If the rendered HTML hash is unchanged, the morph is skipped; a changed evaluated object or handler slot still forces the necessary child prop update.

this.state.a = 1
this.state.b = 2
this.state.c = 3
// one animation-frame render

// same HTML + same render slots
// → skip morph

// same HTML + changed :user object
// → morph so child props update
3 writes → 1 rendersame output → 0 morphs
hash skipping is automatic and requires no memo API

active input · classList sync · scroll · animation

Preserve what the user is doing

Focused input values and checked state are protected from render sync. Class changes use classList rather than replacing the attribute, so running CSS animations survive. Stable nodes keep scroll and selection state.

// while the user types into the focused input:
this.state.server_status = 'saved'

// Fez updates the status elsewhere but preserves:
// - active input value and checked state
// - focus and selection
// - element scroll position
// - running CSS animation classes
typing continuesfocus staysanimation stays
the live DOM, not a recreated tree, remains the source of interaction state

fez:keep subtree · plain fields · controller-only

Three direct-DOM escape hatches

For a frequently updated component with hundreds or thousands of nodes, protect one subtree, store data outside state, or omit the template entirely. Lifecycle, props, CSS, events and cleanup still work.

// 1. reactive shell, protected body
<h3>{state.title}</h3>
<div fez:keep="grid" fez:this="grid"></div>

// 2. plain field: no render
this.rows = []

// 3. no template: pure controller
onMount() {
  this.root.append(this.buildTenThousandRows())
}

patch(i, value) {
  this.cells[i].textContent = value
}
10k rowsdirect textContent updates at vanilla speed
external DOM libraries use the same pattern: mount once, update their nodes directly

10 / 10

Pjax and tooling

The distribution includes progressive page navigation, a component compiler and focused developer tools. They are optional, but they share the same runtime and component model.

window.Pjax · boot gating · start()

Navigation only when invited

window.Pjax is always exposed, but click, popstate and form handlers bind only when the initial page contains a named pjax container. Late containers opt in with Pjax.start().

<main id="pjax" class="pjax">
  ...server-rendered page content...
</main>

// late-injected container
Pjax.start()

// pages without a pjax container keep
// ordinary browser navigation
container foundlinks, history and forms enhanced
Fez backs off if another library already owns window.Pjax

load · refresh · reload · path · last · node · refreshed

Complete navigation API

Navigate, refresh the whole page or one target, bypass cache, inspect the current and previous path and locate the active container. push, replace and query-string helpers cover history changes.

Pjax.load('/users')
Pjax.refresh()
Pjax.refresh('#sidebar')
Pjax.reload({ scroll: false })

Pjax.path()
Pjax.last()
Pjax.node()
Pjax.refreshed()

Pjax.push('/users?page=2')
Pjax.replace('/users?page=3')
Pjax.qs('page', 4)
Pjax.qs('page')
fetch→history→morph→scroll
load options control target, history, replace, scroll, cache, force, form and completion

links · forms · target · refresh · confirm · replace

Declarative navigation attributes

Ordinary links are intercepted automatically. Classes opt out, target attributes replace only one region, refresh attributes re-fetch the current URL, confirmation can be synchronous or async, and forms submit through Pjax.

<a href="/users">Users</a>
<a href="/export" class="no-pjax">Download</a>
<a href="/tab" pjax-target="#panel">Tab</a>
<button pjax-refresh="#panel">Refresh</button>
<a href="/delete" pjax-confirm="Are you sure?">Delete</a>
<a href="/filters" pjax-replace>Filters</a>

<form data-pjax="true">...</form>
<form data-pjax="#panel">...</form>
full swaptarget swapnative opt-outPjax form
the direct class is also accepted as a native-navigation opt-out

pjax:start · pjax:render · before · after · confirm · emit

Cancelable hooks and lifecycle events

Cancel before navigation, customize confirmation, react after full swaps and listen for structured start and render events. Render detail includes origin, destination, status, error, duration, mode and options.

document.addEventListener('pjax:start', event => {})
document.addEventListener('pjax:render', event => {
  console.log(event.detail.from, event.detail.to)
  console.log(event.detail.status, event.detail.error)
  console.log(event.detail.duration, event.detail.mode)
})

Pjax.before = (href, opts) => true
Pjax.after = href => analytics.page(href)
Pjax.confirm = (message, node) => Dialog.confirm(message)
Pjax.emit('app:navigated', { href: Pjax.path() })
start cancelablerender measuredasync confirm
inside a component, this.on('pjax:render', handler) cleans itself up
